name: Ushida
tagline: Tokyo in 26 minutes and Otemachi in 28 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Adachi City, where Tobu and Keisei run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 28 minutes to Otemachi, 40 minutes to Shinjuku, 48 minutes to Shibuya and 40 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 0.9 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 0.9 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from -0.8 m to 3 m, a difference of 3.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 8 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 5 to 10 m. For storm surge, 2 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 10 clinics and 7 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 健和会柳原病院, about 9 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 愛里病院, about 11 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Tobu Skytree Line and Keisei Main Line. The lines are split between operators (Tobu runs 1 line and Keisei runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tobu Skytree Line runs at 142% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 小菅→北千住, which this station is not on. Keisei Main Line runs at 137%. Its busiest stretch is 大神宮下→京成船橋, which this station is likewise not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Horikiri is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Ushida is ahead on the number of lines and the number of medical facilities.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ushida. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Ushida. One-room rents run about ¥10,000 lower.

neighbours.lead: Kita-Senju is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is, but Ushida is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ushida. It reaches Otemachi 6 minutes sooner than Ushida.

goodFor: People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People living alone who want to hold the rent down
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
noiseSources: 墨堤通り (a main road) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road
The nearest big road, 川の手通り, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 2 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 5 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are lightly loaded in the morning.
